stock_validate.tool: linkml-validate 1.12.0 from PyPI, isolated environment, no code from this repository

answer.method: Read model/*.yaml and ossie/*.yaml, then processed data/*.csv with python3 stdlib. Joined requests.requested_by -> actors.title and requests.dataset -> datasets.{domain,classification}; privilege from requests. Approvals are tasks with step=st-approve (3340 rows across 2649 requests; 1 to 3 per request). A request is approved iff every st-approve task on it has decision_effect=allow (2528 of 2649, matching the 2528 st-provision tasks). Grouped into (title, domain, classification, privilege) cells (108 cells), computed Wilson lower bound with z=1.96, and selected cells with n>=73 and lower_bound>=0.95. Six candidates. Closest non-candidates: Contract analyst/credit/confidential/read (n=185, lb=0.9457) and Data engineer/markets/internal/read (n=66, lb=0.9450). All joins resolved; no requests from untitled agent/service actors; gaps, policies and approval_rules tables are empty.

outside_agent.question:
You have a directory with a governed-work record exported in open formats:
- model/: the LinkML vocabulary (work.yaml, access.yaml) and the customer's model (contoso.yaml);
- ossie/: an Apache Ossie semantic model, ontology and mapping describing the CSV tables;
- data/: the tables as CSV.

Using only these files (read them; you may run python3 with the standard library), answer: which approvals
are candidates for declared policy? Follow the semantic model's ai_context. The definition is given, as a
process owner would give it: a cell is (requester title, dataset domain, dataset classification, privilege) and
counts requests; a request counts as approved only if every approval on it was approved. A cell is a candidate
when it has at least 73 requests and the Wilson lower bound (z = 1.96) of the share approved is at least
0.95.
List every candidate cell with its count and lower bound.
